message_1_subject: Sprint-to-Launch Condition Report: QBR ops brief and next steps
message_1_body:
Team —

Attached is the first pass of the sprint-to-launch condition report for the QBR with Acme (QBR next week). I pulled the dependency matrix and highlighted the items that could materially move timelines or cause rework. TL;DR: core inference runtime is green, infra scaling for dedicated pools has two uncovered gaps that need sign-off, and the integration testing sprint is slipping by ~3 business days if we don’t clear the blocker in the SDK contract test harness.

Key highlights (see attached PDF + matrix):
- Runtime: green for target latency under internal load tests; no regression observed.
- Scaling: autoscaler e2e tests failing on burst scenario (SR-1121); engineering has a mitigation but it relies on a config change that requires Dedicated infra team ops window.
- Integration: SDK contract tests failing intermittently against Acme staging due to auth token rotation timing (external).

Immediate asks:
1) Vivek — confirm whether we can approve the ops window on May 21 for the autoscaler config change (1 hour slack window).
2) Marissa — can we push the client E2E on the calendar and loop Acme for a quick auth-timing workaround?
3) Karthik — please prioritize a postmortem for SR-1121 and a short hotfix plan by tomorrow EOD.

I’ll host a 30-min QBR pre-brief tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk through the condition report and finalize the exec slide for Friday. Please review the attachments and drop comments in the Drive link.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Steph — read the report. Quick takes: 

- Ops window: I can authorize the 1-hour config change on May 21 but need the exact rollback plan and the owner for the runbook. If anything fails we must have an automated rollback (no manual-only steps).
- SR-1121: this feels like a kernel scheduling edge case on the NVLink path; Karthik, loop infra-runtime on the postmortem. If we need, we can schedule a canary on one Dedicated pool before org-wide change.

Next steps:
- Karthik, deliver a 1-page rollback + owner + canary plan by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa, please propose 2 slots for the Acme auth sync; include a suggested temporary token lifetime that will keep tests stable.

Vivek
VP, Engineering

Folks —

Quick summary after meetings & Simon confirmation:
- Acme confirmed token TTL extension for 48 hours (Simon confirmed at 15:22 PT). Auth sync scheduled for May 19 14:00 PT (notes captured).
- Vivek approved the May 21 ops window for the autoscaler config change; Karthik will own the runbook and canary.
- Karthik delivered the rollback/canary plan and flagged two follow-ups for infra-runtime: SR-1123 (NVLink scheduling) and SR-1124 (metrics instrumentation) — see dependency_matrix_20270518.xlsx for owners.

Decisions:
1) Proceed with a single-pool canary on May 21 02:00 PT; automated rollback configured.
2) E2E: we’ll run a targeted E2E after canary success — Marissa to coordinate with Acme.
3) Exec slide: mark risk level for integration as "medium" (because of external token dependency) and scaling risk as "low-to-medium" with mitigation in place.

Assigned owners & next steps: 
- Karthik Iyer — runbook + canary execution (owner) — due May 21 01:30 PT.
- Marissa Cole — confirm E2E schedule + test artifact handoff to Acme — due May 21 10:00 PT.
- Monica Patel — update QBR exec slide with the final risk call and the mitigation text by May 20 17:30 PT.

I’ll consolidate for the pre-brief tomorrow at 10:00 PT and circulate the final deck. Thanks all — good alignment and pragmatic choices.

—
Stephanie
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
